title: Honest but Wrong: Formalizing Retraction in the Ethics of Speech Acts
abstract: arXiv:2611.34011v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: A speaker who asserts honestly may later discover that its assertion was false. Such erroneous truths are not lies, yet they raise the question of whether, and on which moral grounds, the speaker must retract them. Using the FIPA-ACL performative disconfirm, we extend a belief-based framework that evaluates speech acts under deontologism and consequentialism to the case of retraction. We prove that the honesty duty of deontologism, which bears on utterances when they are made, never requires retracting an erroneous truth, and add a persistent one, which forbids letting the addressee believe what the speaker no longer believes. On a legal-advice case implemented in Answer Set Programming, we show that deontologism and consequentialism both require the retraction, but that consequentialism no longer does once it comes too late to prevent harm.

translated_title: 诚实但错误：言语行为伦理学中撤回的形式化
translated_abstract: 一个诚实作出断言的说话者可能在后来发现其断言是错误的。这种“错误的真相”并非谎言，却引发了一个问题：说话者是否必须撤回它们，以及基于何种道德理由。我们利用FIPA-ACL言语行为中的disconfirm（否认），将一个基于信念的、在义务论与后果论下评估言语行为的框架扩展到撤回的情形。我们证明，义务论的诚实义务——该义务在话语发出时生效——从不要求撤回错误的真相；并新增了一条持续性义务，禁止让受话者继续相信说话者自己已不再相信的内容。在一个用答案集编程实现的法律咨询案例中，我们表明义务论与后果论都要求撤回，但一旦撤回已来不及防止损害，后果论便不再提出此要求。
tldr: 该论文将言语行为伦理学中的“撤回”形式化，证明了义务论的诚实义务从不要求撤回“错误的真相”，并新增一条持续性义务禁止让受话者相信说话者已不再相信的内容，同时通过法律咨询案例表明后果论仅在撤回仍能防止损害时才要求撤回。
en_tdlr: This paper formalizes retraction in the ethics of speech acts, proving that deontological honesty never requires retracting an erroneous truth, adding a persistent duty forbidding the addressee to keep believing what the speaker no longer believes, and showing through a legal-advice case that consequentialism demands retraction only when it can still prevent harm.
